hints: Focus on the phrase maintain the genetic composition. It means the two daughter cells must end up genetically identical to the parent and to each other.
Think in two parts: first you must make an exact copy of all the DNA, then you must share those copies out exactly equally, one set to each pole.
walkthrough:
**What does maintain mean here?**

Mitosis is about making identical copies. No loss and no gain of genes.

That needs two jobs: copy everything exactly, then split it exactly equally.

**Check statement 2 first**

Before mitosis, in interphase (S phase), all DNA replicates.

Each chromosome makes two identical sister chromatids. Without this, there would not be enough DNA for two identical cells. So 2 is essential.

**Check statements 1 and 3**

In anaphase, the centromere divides longitudinally. This lets the two sister chromatids separate.

Then spindle fibres pull one chromatid of each pair to opposite poles. This guarantees each new nucleus gets one complete, identical set. So 1 and 3 are both essential.

Since 1, 2 and 3 all help, the answer is A.

options.A: Correct, because exact replication (2) plus exact splitting by centromere division (1) and movement to opposite poles (3) together produce two genetically identical cells.
options.B: Incorrect, because it leaves out 2. Without prior DNA replication there would be no identical copies to share out.
options.C: Incorrect, because centromere division alone is not enough. You also need replication to make the copies and poleward movement to distribute them.
options.D: Incorrect, because it leaves out 1. Longitudinal division of the centromere is what frees the sister chromatids so they can be pulled apart equally.
